16. It is on record that Birendra Kumar Dey left Bangladesh in 1958 and Rabindra Kumar Dey was staying in Bangladesh. SA Khatian, Ext. 8 was prepared in the year 1960-62 in the name of Rabindra. Municipal assessment holding, Ext. 3 was also made in the name of Rabindra Kumar Dey in the year 1962-63. The receipt of municipal taxes, Ext. 4 series show that taxes were paid by Rabindra Kumar Dey in the year 1962-63, Exts. 5-5A, rent receipts show payment of rent by vendor. Rabindra Kumar Dey after preparation of SA Khatian, Ext. 8. The learned Single Judge found that these documents are all prior to 1965 before the Indo-Pak War and before anybody''s contemplation of coming into force of the Enemy Property Law in this country. The learned Single Judge further found from Ext. 6, that defendant No. 5 (appellant in Civil Appeal No. 23 of 1997) paid rent to Birendra Kumar Dey as monthly tenant. Thereafter he paid rent to Rabindra Kumar Dey and his father. Thus, the learned Single Judge found that defendant No. 5 was aware that Rabindra Kumar Dey was the real owner and to him he was paying rent. It is also on record that defendant No. 5 was paying rent to the plaintiff admitting him as owner after his purchase from Rabindra Kumar Dey. Ext. 7 to 7 (f) are the agreements of the tenants with the plaintiff" as the landlord. Ext 10 also showed that other tenants filed petition admitting that they were tenants under defendant No. 4. Defendant No. 5 also admitted in his cross-examination that he paid rent to the plaintiff. Ext. 10 showed that other tenants filed petition admitting that they were tenants under defendant No. 4 and they never denied that the plaintiff''s vendor was not the real owner. The rent-receipts and tax receipts submitted by the plaintiff were found by the appellate Court to have been initially paid in the name of defendant No. 3 who was, in fact, the benamder and subsequently all these documents were corrected in the name of defendant No. 4, the real owner. 

 17. The lower appellate Court held that there was no paper to support the question of benami from 1944 till the preparation of SA Khatian in the name of Rabindra Kumar Dey and consequently disbelieved the story of benami. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division considered the oral evidence in this regard and believed the story of benami and found that the lower appellate Court without considering the material evidence both oral and documentary and on wrong assumptions disbelieved the case of benami. Herein we will consider the relevant evidence of benami on which the learned Single Judge has made reliance in his judgment after due consideration of the evidence of PW 2 Aboni Mohan Dey. The learned Single Judge held as follows: 

 18. The learned Single Judge also reversed the finding of the lower appellate Court that the preparation of SA Khatian No. 83, Exhibit 8, municipal assessment in 1961-62 are all collusively done in 1960-61 prior to 1965 when enemy property Ordinance came into force. The learned Single Judge held that it was a mere presumption of the lower appellate Court to hold that in order to save the property from being treated as enemy property all these corrections of SA Khatian and municipal Assessment Register were made. The learned Single Judge also reversed the finding of the lower appellate Court with regard to the plaintiff''s kabala Ext. 1(A) dated 22-11-63 executed by defendant No. 4 by holding that there was no recital that defendant No.4 was the real owner and his brother Birendra defendant No. 3 was simply a name lender. The property is being sold by the real owner and this omission is not very material. Rabindra Kumar Dey possessed the property and let it out to tenants and tenants paid rent to Rabindra Kumar Dey and, as such, Rabindra Kumar Dey treated the property as his own property for all practical purposes. Further, in the sale deed dated 22-11-63 there is a clear recital by vendor Rabindra Kumar Dey that he purchased the property with his own money and for his own interest and owning in his own right. This recital also indirectly reflects that the property was in the benami of his brother. 

 20. The defendants adduced two witnesses, namely, DW 1 Tahsilder and DW 2 Abdul Karim (defendant No. 5), a lessee under the vested property authority. DW 1 testified that in the census list of 1967 the disputed property was enlisted as enemy property but he could not produce any paper. He joined office in 1976 for the first time and he only deposed that SA Khatian which was prepared in 1961-62 was wrong. DW 2 Abdul Karim said in his cross-examination that he paid rents to Barindra but he could not produce any rent receipts on the plea that those were burnt. He admitted that on his application Government has granted lease to him and before that he used to pay rent to the plaintiff. This is all the oral evidence on record on behalf of the defendants.
